question: According to 2011 Census, the urban-rural population ratio in India was about:
solution:
The correct answer is __**31 ∶ 69**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census, the urban-rural population ratio in India was about **31 ∶ 69**.
 
• This ratio indicates that approximately 31% of India's population lived in urban areas while 69% resided in rural areas.
 
• The data reflects the distribution of population across different regions, highlighting the predominance of rural habitation in India.
 
• Urbanization trends have been gradually increasing, but a significant portion of the population still remains in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **2011 Census** was the 15th Census of India since 1871 and was conducted in two phases: house listing and population enumeration.
 
• During the Census, various demographic parameters such as population size, density, growth, and urban-rural distribution were collected.
 
• The information collected helps in planning and formulation of policies for economic and social development.
 
• Census data is crucial for the allocation of resources and representation in legislative bodies.
 
• India's Census is one of the largest administrative exercises in the world, involving millions of enumerators and extensive fieldwork.
 
• The next Census in India is scheduled to be conducted in 2021, which will provide updated demographic data.
